title: Assistant Professor of Economics
description:
Work Authorization and Immigration Sponsorship

Wichita State University may be able to sponsor certain faculty
positions for employment-based immigration status where authorized
by the hiring department and university policy. Sponsorship
eligibility varies by faculty position and will be identified in
the individual job posting.

For faculty positions eligible for sponsorship, international
candidates generally must be eligible for sponsorship in a visa
classification compatible with the faculty position. For tenured
and tenure-track faculty appointments, visa classifications
incompatible with such appointments include F-1 Optional Practical
Training (OPT), J-1 Research Scholar, and J-1 Academic Training
statuses.

Department: Barton School of Business - Department of
Marketing & Economics

Campus Location: Wichita, KS - WSU Main Campus

Hire Type: Full Time

Pay: Salary set at $109,535/yr

Work Schedule: Dependent on teaching assignment and research
program needs;work is performed on-site and in person.

Export Compliance Requirement: No export control
requirement.

Job Story

Candidates will have an exciting opportunity to contribute to the
future of economics education and research at Wichita State
University. The position will play an important role in
strengthening undergraduate and graduate economics education,
producing academic research that advances knowledge, and
contributing to innovative academic and applied-learning
initiatives that connect economics with industry and the broader
community. Wichita State University is classified as a high
research activity institution and provides faculty with
opportunities and institutional support for research,
interdisciplinary collaboration, external funding, and
industry-engaged scholarship.

The Department of Economics in the W. Frank Barton School of
Business at Wichita State University invites applications for a
nine-month, tenure-track position as Assistant Professor of
Economics, beginning Fall 2027.

You will teach undergraduate and graduate courses, establish clear
learning objectives, develop curriculum and instructional materials
that accomplish those objectives, and provide students with the
support needed to succeed. We welcome candidates who can contribute
expertise in economics and statistics and build productive
professional relationships within the community and across the
university.

Wichita State University places applied learning at the center of
student experience. Every degree program at Wichita State includes
a guaranteed applied learning or research experience, providing
students with opportunities to develop relevant professional skills
and meaningful experience before graduation. The successful
candidate will have opportunities to integrate these experiences
into economics education through applied projects with industry,
case studies, research, and engagement with local businesses and
the larger community.

Job Summary

Teach courses at the undergraduate and graduate levels using
various instructional deliveries (e.g., traditional (face-to-face),
hybrid, and fully online). To foster applied learning into the
course design and engage with industry and local business community
applied projects. To advance knowledge through scholarly activities
(e.g., active involvement in committees, student mentorship,
recruitment and retention initiative, outreach activities,
etc.)

Essential Functions

Meet expectations for research, teaching, and service as set forth
by the department and college.

Job Duties

The successful candidate will be expected to:

1. Teaching: Teach two courses per semester (four courses per
academic year) at the undergraduate and graduate levels, with
courses offered in face-to-face, hybrid, blended, and fully online
formats. Each course is three credit hours. Teaching assignments
may include, depending on the candidate's expertise and program
needs, Principles of Microeconomics, Labor Economics, Business
Statistics, and related courses with the opportunity to develop
courses in the candidate's area of expertise. The successful
candidate will establish key objectives for classes, develop
curriculum and syllabi, present course material through lectures
and learning activities, and answer students' questions and provide
support to help them succeed.

2. Applied Learning and Community Engagement: Foster applied
learning in course design by developing meaningful opportunities
for students to engage with industry, local businesses, and the
larger community through applied projects, case studies,
professional engagement, and other experiential learning
activities.

3. Research: Develop and maintain an active and sustainable program
of academic research consistent with AACSB Scholarly Academic (SA)
expectations and the requirements for tenure and promotion at the
Barton School of Business. The successful candidate will be
expected to publish high-quality scholarly research in respected
and leading economics or related academic journals and advance
knowledge through sustained scholarly activity.

4. Service and Engagement: Contribute meaningful service to the
department, Barton School of Business, university, profession, and
local community. Service may include active involvement in
committees, student mentorship, student recruitment and retention
initiatives, professional organizations, outreach activities, and
other activities that advance the mission of the department and
school.

Required Education and Experience:

Terminal degree in direct field
Teaching experience

Faculty Requirements

A Ph.D. in Economics from an accredited institution.
Applicants who are at an advanced stage of their doctoral studies
(ABD) will be considered if they provide strong evidence that all
degree requirements will be completed prior to the June 2027.
Evidence of an established record of scholarly research or a
strong research pipeline with demonstrated ability or potential to
publish in high-quality economics or related academic
journals.
Evidence of, or demonstrated potential for, effective teaching
in economics at the undergraduate and graduate levels. Evidence may
include teaching evaluations, curriculum or course development,
applied-learning activities, experience with face-to-face, hybrid,
blended, or fully online instruction, or other indicators of
teaching effectiveness.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

Knowledge of economics and statistics.
Ability to build professional relationships within the
community and across the university at all levels.
Ability to provide instruction of curriculum to a variety of
learners.
Commitment to collaborative processes and environments.

Preferred Qualifications:

Research and/or teaching interests in labor economics and/or
environmental economics.
Use of empirical methods, econometric techniques, or data-intensive
approaches to address applied economic questions.

Additional Information:

REQUIRED MATERIALS
1. Cover Letter/Letter of application addressing how the
candidate’s qualifications and experience align with the
position.
2. Teaching Statement: A statement (1-2 pages) describing teaching
approach/philosophy and experience (including course topics the
candidate can teach, mentoring experience, and any evidence of
teaching effectiveness).
3. Research Statement: A statement (1-2 pages) describing research
approach/philosophy and experience.

A priority deadline for application review is October 31, 2026. The
appointment for the position is August 2027.

Physical Requirements:

Ability to remain in a stationary position – Frequent 60-90%;
Ability to operate a computer and other office equipment including
but not limited to phone, printers, copiers, and calculators –
Frequent 60-90%
